genxml.title: Brooktree Bt457 RAMDAC as wired on the Express board (three chips, one per colour)
genxml.doc: Three single-colour 5:1 multiplexed RAMDACs behind the five XMAP5 chips: red, green and blue, each with its own four-port window. Offsets are within one chip's window; the red, green and blue windows are 0x20 bytes apart (addresses in the README). Each port is one byte at the first byte of a 4-byte stride, so a big-endian CPU addresses the most significant lane. The port numbers follow the datasheet's C1 and C0 inputs: the stride bit 2 is C0 and bit 3 is C1. Grades: established means stated by the published Bt457/Bt458 datasheet or read in full in the shipped Indigo driver or PROM; inferred means a reasoned reading; unknown means nothing settles it. [public] marks the datasheet, [binary] a shipped binary. The datasheet says the command, read-mask, blink-mask and test registers are not initialised at power-up; this page gives no reset values. Nothing was read on a board. Prose in devices/bt457/README.md.

struct.name: ADDR
struct.doc: Address register. Written before every register or palette access; after a palette or overlay access it advances (palette wraps to 0 after 255, overlay goes to 4 after overlay 3, control registers do not advance it). [public] [binary] A qtest can discriminate: write 255 to addr, write two bytes to palette, check the address wrapped to 0 then 1.

struct.name: PALETTE
struct.doc: Colour palette RAM data. The three chips are addressed separately, so the board uses the datasheet's normal mode: one byte write stores one colour component of the addressed entry and the address advances. [public] [binary]

struct.name: CTRL
struct.doc: Control register data: the register picked by addr (read mask, blink mask, command, test) is read or written here and addr does not advance. [public] [binary] Gr2BlankScreen writes the read mask this way, ctrl 0 to blank and 255 to unblank, after addr 4, in all three chips.

struct.name: OVERLAY
struct.doc: Overlay colour data, entries 0 to 3 selected by addr. Init writes four bytes 0 to 3 after setting addr to 0. [public] [binary]

struct.name: COMMAND
struct.doc: Command register fields, from the datasheet. The board writes 0xc1.
